  "text": "Mara held the photograph toward the bell’s weak light. The crossed-out letters were still there, pressed deep into the paper. She could make out an M, then the long stroke of an r.

The pole cracked. The harbor master leaned his shoulder against it, but the gate opened the width of a finger.

“Don’t,” the woman said.

Mara looked at the girl in the photograph. She stood apart from the other children, one hand hidden behind her back. Mara turned the picture sideways. Beneath that hand, almost lost in the gray stone, was a small white shell.

She had kept a shell like it for years. It was in her coat pocket now.

Mara took it out. The eye beyond the tear followed her hand.

“I remember the photograph,” she said. “Someone told us not to move.”

The man from the boat stood up too quickly. “You weren’t there.”

“I was afraid of the bell.” Mara ran her thumb over the shell’s ridged edge. “You held it for me until it stopped.”

His face changed. He looked at the woman, who had begun to cry without making a sound.

The gate shuddered. Mara pressed the shell into the narrow opening. A hand reached for it—small, pale, and marked across the palm by an old cut. Mara had the same scar.

The hand closed around the shell. For a moment it held on to Mara’s fingers too. Then it withdrew.

The bolt slid back into place. Across the water, the bell gave one last, uneven note.

Mara turned the photograph over again. The torn name was legible now. It was hers."
